project.name: home-assistant-codex-persistence
project.goal: Keep the Codex home, native sessions, sign-in, configuration, GitHub CLI sign-in, and required CLI programs outside the replaceable Studio Code Server container; reconnect them automatically at every add-on start; and start the persisted GitHub CLI without APT or network access.
project.users: Home Assistant operators using Studio Code Server, Codex, and GitHub CLI
project.acceptance_owner: Operator of the Home Assistant reference system

intake.success_example: After a supported lifecycle event, an existing native Codex session remains resumable, both sign-ins remain valid, projects and the private memory file remain unchanged, the authentication audit reports no BLOCK, gh and github-cli are absent from packages, unrelated packages remain unchanged, and the persisted gh starts without APT or network access.
intake.systems: Home Assistant Supervisor, Studio Code Server, the Codex extension and Codex CLI, GitHub CLI, persistent add-on storage, a persistent workspace, and the install, boot, and audit script.
intake.confidential_data: Codex and GitHub credentials, native session files, databases, private runtime profiles, and real memory content. They remain local in protected persistent storage and never enter Git or ordinary unprotected mirrors.

interfaces.purpose: A one-time install persists and verifies the Codex home, GitHub CLI configuration, and CLI programs. After the gh copy and ready generation are verified, the same Supervisor update removes only gh and github-cli from packages, preserves unrelated packages and commands, and places boot first. Automatic boot restores the expected links before code-server without upgrading programs. Audit checks the state without modifying it.
interfaces.failure: Missing installation, unstable sources, damaged programs, unexpected links, or competing non-empty paths cause BLOCK. Existing state is never overwritten or merged automatically. Unrelated packages that remain configured may still require APT or network access before init_commands.

states.states: not installed, ready, active, or blocked
states.safe_state: For every deviation, existing state remains unchanged and startup is blocked with a specific diagnostic.

storage.workspace_rule: Projects and the real memory file reside in a persistent workspace under /config.
storage.repository_role: Git and GitHub contain only the version-controlled installation project. They are neither runtime persistence nor backup; the private runtime resides under HACP_RUNTIME_ROOT and the real local MEMORY.md resides in the persistent workspace.
storage.github_cli_package_lifecycle: gh is a one-time bootstrap package. After persistence has been verified, install removes only gh and github-cli from packages while preserving unrelated packages. For the persisted gh, boot requires no APT or network access and performs no upgrade.

open_items.text: Record Home Assistant host-reboot evidence under TC-012.
Test a future real add-on update or container recreation as a TC-012 regression event.
Design and verify the persisted CLI upgrade and rollback workflow described by BL-005.

assumptions.text: The configured target path remains persistent across add-on restart, update, and container recreation.
init_commands run with the required permissions before code-server at every add-on start.
Studio Code and extensions remain independently persistent under /data/vscode.
The add-on processes a non-empty packages list through APT before init_commands; an empty list skips this step.

risks.text: A restart before a successful install can lose state that exists only under /root.
A session or database source that changes during copying is inconsistent and must cause a block.
Private runtime data or real memory content must not enter Git, logs, or ordinary unprotected mirrors.
Persisted provider sign-ins can expire or be revoked server-side.
Container persistence does not replace an encrypted backup of persistent Home Assistant storage.
Unrelated add-on packages that remain configured may require APT or network access before init_commands and prevent fully offline startup.
Persisted CLI programs may become outdated or incompatible with a later container; upgrades must use the planned verified BL-005 workflow and never run during boot.
